candidate.educational_objective: Explain the local protective action of sucralfate.

options.A: It acts locally by forming an ulcer-adherent complex that covers the ulcer site and helps protect it from acid, pepsin, and bile salts.
options.B: It is primarily absorbed systemically and permanently stops gastric acid secretion.
options.C: It accelerates gastric emptying through dopamine-2 receptor antagonism.
options.D: It eradicates Helicobacter pylori as a single-agent antibiotic.

candidate.rationale: Sucralfate is minimally absorbed and acts locally. Labeling describes formation of an ulcer-adherent complex that covers the ulcer site and helps protect it against further attack by acid, pepsin, and bile salts.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Sucralfate acts locally by adhering to the ulcer site and creating a protective barrier.
candidate.source_locator: Clinical Pharmacology—local action; ulcer-adherent complex; barrier against acid, pepsin, and bile salts
candidate.stem: Which statement best explains how sucralfate helps an active duodenal ulcer?
